pages.title: How to Use This Analysis
pages.text:
How to Use This Analysis

The 3-out-of-4 Reality
The safest strategy is not to memorize isolated questions. Each main question often mixes 2-4 subtopics. The eight sets
below are preparation clusters built from repeated question families, so mastering one set gives coverage across multiple
historical question numbers.

FASTEST EXAM STRATEGY
Preparation order                                              Set

Section A - Priority 1                                         A1 Thermal Comfort & Heat Exchange

Section A - Priority 2                                         A2 Ventilation & Repeating Numericals

Section A - Priority 3                                         A3 Microclimate / Envelope / Shading

Section A - Backup                                             A4 Climate-Context + Climate-Friendly Construction

Section B - Priority 1                                         B1 Global Climatic Factors & Wind System

Section B - Priority 2                                         B3 Regional / Site / Urban Climate

Section B - Priority 3                                         B2 Tropical Climate

Section B - Backup                                             B4 Elements / Measurement / Basic Thermal Response

Important Warning
Do not completely skip the 4th set. From 2021 onward, main questions are highly mixed. If time is short, prepare the first 3
sets deeply and keep a one-page emergency revision sheet for Set 4.

DATA SCOPE AND METHOD
  Eight regular final-term papers are present in the supplied question bank: 2016, 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023
  and 2024. A 2019 paper is not present in the uploaded bank.
  The 2020 paper is a reduced 120-mark paper with only three main questions per section. It is counted for topic
  presence, but not treated as a normal four-question structure.
  Frequency means a direct question or a close conceptual variant appeared in that paper. It is not a claim that the
  wording was identical.
  Historical papers sometimes place the two teachers' content under different printed section labels. Therefore this
  analysis maps questions to the CURRENT uploaded Section A / Section B lecture blocks by topic, not blindly by the
  old printed section heading.
  Overlapping topics (especially site climate and thermal comfort) are assigned according to the dominant lecture
  framing and question style.

pages.title: Question-Type Analysis
pages.text:
Question-Type Analysis

1. HIGH-PRIORITY THEORY / DISCUSSION QUESTIONS
  A1: Factors of climatic comfort; thermal comfort ideas; human body heat exchange; heat loss in climatic situations;
  designer responsibilities; comfort indices.
  A3: Microclimate design; building-envelope response; spacing and openings; effective shading and seasonal solar
  control.
  A4: Climate-context-comfort; climate vs environment; Khana; Vitruvius; green/sustainable building; tube house; rat-
  trap bond.
  B1: Earth-sun relationship, axial tilt, radiation, earth thermal balance, global wind pattern, ITCZ, Coriolis force,
  westerlies/polar winds.
  B2: Tropical climate classification; warm-humid/hot-dry/composite climates; passive control and climatic design
  response.
  B3: Regional/site/urban climate; factor hierarchy; site-design process; urban climate deviation.
  B4: Climatic elements, measurement methods, driving rain, climatic data interpretation and basic thermal response.

2. PROOF / DERIVATION / ANALYTICAL-EQUATION LIST

 Important
 The supplied papers contain very few formal mathematical "proofs". What repeatedly appears are equations,
 relationships, mechanisms and analytical derivations. Prepare the following as derivation-style items.

  Thermal balance equation of the human body and interpretation of imbalance.
  RH-AH-SH relationship: RH = (AH / SH) x 100%, with numerical use.
  Air change / ventilation expressions and heat loss due to air change.
  Driving Rain Index: rainfall x annual average wind speed; exposure classification.
  Cosine law for incident solar radiation and its building-design applications.
  Solar shading geometry: solar altitude/azimuth, horizontal and vertical shadow angles, effective projection and
  incidence angle.
  Earth thermal balance / incoming vs outgoing radiation mechanism.
  Heat-transfer logic through conduction, convection, radiation and evaporation.

3. NUMERICAL PROBLEM LIST - PRIORITY ORDER
  S: Air-space / air-change heat-loss numerical (2021-2024).
  S: Fire-shelter capacity and fresh-air safety numerical (2021-2024).
  S: Laboratory ventilation suitability / power-failure numerical (2021-2024).
  S: Solar shading projection + angle of incidence (2023-2024).
  A: Relative humidity from AH and SH (2020-2021).
  A: Ventilation requirement in m3/s, L/s and ACH.
  B: DRI calculation and exposure classification (concept + simple calculation).

pages.title: Sketch & Diagram Bank
pages.text:
Sketch & Diagram Bank

DO NOT ENTER THE EXAM WITHOUT THESE
  Global wind belts + pressure belts + ITCZ.
  Earth-sun relationship and axial tilt / seasonal sun position.
  Earth thermal-balance diagram.
  Human body heat exchange: conduction, convection, radiation, evaporation.
  Heat-loss/gain processes under different climatic situations.
  Hot-dry vs warm-humid building form / spacing sketches.
  Building envelope response: roof, wall, window/opening.
  Horizontal, vertical and combined shading devices.
  Summer vs winter overhang/lofty porch sun control.
  Solar-shading plan for window orientation.
  Cross-ventilation / opening-position sketches.
  Rat-trap bond section/brick arrangement.
  Tube-house section and air-movement principle.
  Stevenson screen.
  Wind-frequency graph / wind rose.

Sketch rule
Use clean labels, arrows and a one-line design implication under each figure. A simple accurate sketch is more valuable
than an artistic drawing.

pages.title: 3-Out-of-4 Preparation Strategy
pages.text:
3-Out-of-4 Preparation Strategy

 If you have enough time
 Prepare all four sets in each section. This is the only fully safe approach because recent papers deliberately mix subtopics.

IF TIME IS LIMITED - SECTION A
  1) MASTER A1 completely: theory + diagrams + ET/CET/EW/OT.
  2) MASTER A2 numericals: practice at least one air-change, one shelter and one lab problem without notes.
  3) MASTER A3 design: envelope + microclimate + shading sketches; practice one solar-shading numerical.
  4) BACKUP A4: memorize climate-context-comfort, Khana, tube house, rat-trap bond and sustainability definitions.

IF TIME IS LIMITED - SECTION B
  1) MASTER B1 completely: earth-sun, radiation, heat balance and world winds.
  2) MASTER B3: factor hierarchy + site design + urban climate deviation.
  3) MASTER B2: tropical classification + warm-humid vs hot-dry + design response.
  4) BACKUP B4: DRI, Stevenson screen, wind graph, climatic measurement and short thermal notes.

 Last-night rule
 Do not spend the last night reading entire reference books. Use the set pages in this analysis as the map, then open the
 matching class slide/note only for diagrams, exact formulas and teacher-specific wording.

RECOMMENDED REVISION CYCLE
  Day 1: A1 + B1 (highest-recurrence theory).
  Day 2: A2 + B3 (numerical + site climate).
  Day 3: A3 + B2 (design/sketch + tropical climate).
  Day 4: A4 + B4 (backup sets + short notes).
  Final revision: numericals, diagrams, comparison tables, then only the S-priority question families.

Source Map & Reliability Notes

PRIMARY FREQUENCY SOURCE
  Climate and Architectural Design QB (16-24).pdf - used to identify year-by-year recurrence, marks and recent trends.

SECTION A MAPPING / CROSS-CHECK
  Qs Analysis- Shahriar Sir.pdf - used as a secondary lecture-wise map, then cross-checked against the original regular
  papers.
  Section A lecture slides (Lectures 1-11) and Shahriar Sir class notes - used to determine current topic boundaries
  and terminology.

SECTION B MAPPING / CROSS-CHECK
  Section B lecture slides: Introduction, Global Climatic Factors, Elements of Climate, Tropical Climate, Site Climate
  and Thermal Comfort.
  Billah Sir / Abu Safayet Sir notes - used to align the current Section B syllabus with past questions.

REFERENCE BOOKS
  Manual of Tropical Housing and Building: Climatic Design - used only as a reference map for standard topic
  structure and diagrams.
  A Text Book of Climate & Design for the Built-form Designers (Bijon B. Sharma and Falguni Mallick) - used only for
  topic terminology and deeper reference support.

 Reliability note
 Question frequency is based on the uploaded regular papers, not on the student analysis. The student analysis was treated
 as a secondary guide. Where old exam section labels conflict with the current uploaded teacher-section split, topic content
 controls the mapping.

                                            END OF ANALYSIS
